shorts.title: Exit Ticket #1: Evaluating g(-1) & Binomial Shift g(x - 4)
shorts.subtitle: Given g(x) = 2x² - 3x + 7
shorts.hook: Evaluate g(negative 1) and g(x minus 4) step-by-step with proper notation!
shorts.coreQuestion: How do you evaluate a quadratic function with a negative integer input versus a variable binomial input?

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: Welcome Bobcats! Let's solve M090 3.0 to 3.3 Exit Ticket Problem #1: given g of x equals 2x squared minus 3x plus 7, evaluate g of negative 1 and g of x minus 4.

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: For Part A, wrap negative 1 in protective parentheses! g of negative 1 equals 2 times negative 1 squared, minus 3 times negative 1, plus 7.

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: Exponents first: negative 1 squared is positive 1. 2 times 1 is 2. Then negative 3 times negative 1 gives positive 3. 2 plus 3 plus 7 equals 12!

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: For Part B, replace every x with the quantity x minus 4! We write 2 times the quantity x minus 4 squared, minus 3 times the quantity x minus 4, plus 7.

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: Expand x minus 4 squared to get x squared minus 8x plus 16. Multiply by 2: 2x squared minus 16x plus 32.

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: Distribute negative 3 to get negative 3x plus 12. Combine all like terms: 2x squared minus 19x plus 51! Box your answers: 12 and 2x squared minus 19x plus 51!

shorts.title: Exit Ticket #2: Vertex & x-Intercepts of f(x) = 3x² - 12x
shorts.subtitle: Missing Constant Parabola (c = 0)
shorts.hook: When constant c equals 0, find the vertex and x intercepts in under 45 seconds!
shorts.coreQuestion: How do you find the vertex using x = -b/(2a) and solve for x intercepts by factoring out the GCF?

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: On Exit Ticket Problem #2, we examine f of x equals 3x squared minus 12x. Notice constant c is 0!

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: For Part A, find the vertex! a equals 3, b equals negative 12. Using x equals negative b over 2a, we get negative negative 12 over 2 times 3.

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: Positive 12 over 6 equals 2! Now evaluate f of 2: 3 times 2 squared minus 12 times 2. That is 3 times 4 minus 24, giving 12 minus 24, which is negative 12! The vertex is 2, negative 12!

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: For Part B, find the x intercepts! Set 3x squared minus 12x equal to 0. Factor out the greatest common factor 3x: 3x times the quantity x minus 4 equals 0!

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: Set each factor to zero: 3x equals 0 gives x equals 0. And x minus 4 equals 0 gives x equals 4!

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: Our x intercepts are 0, 0 and 4, 0! Notice the center is halfway at x equals 2, exactly matching our vertex!

shorts.title: Exit Ticket #3: Vertex & Square Root Property for f(x) = 3x² - 12
shorts.subtitle: Missing Linear Term (b = 0)
shorts.hook: Middle term b equals 0? Use the Square Root Property to find the roots in 15 seconds!
shorts.coreQuestion: Why does a missing middle term place the vertex on the y axis and create symmetric plus-or-minus roots?

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: Exit Ticket Problem #3 contrasts beautifully with Problem #2: here f of x equals 3x squared minus 12. Notice the middle term b is 0!

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: For Part A, find the vertex! Since b equals 0, x sub v equals negative 0 over 2 times 3, which is 0! Plugging in 0 gives f of 0 equals negative 12!

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: The vertex is 0, negative 12, resting directly on the y axis! Part B asks for the x intercepts.

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: Set 3x squared minus 12 equal to 0. Add 12 to both sides: 3x squared equals 12! Divide both sides by 3 to isolate x squared: x squared equals 4!

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: Now apply the Square Root Property: x equals plus or minus the square root of 4, which gives x equals plus or minus 2!

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: Write the x intercepts as ordered pairs: 2, 0 and negative 2, 0! The roots are positive 2 and negative 2, symmetric around the origin!

shorts.title: Exit Ticket #4: Vertex Form Features of f(x) = -5(x + 3)² + 180
shorts.subtitle: Vertex Form with a Negative Leading Coefficient
shorts.hook: Vertex form gives the peak instantly! Watch how to find intercepts without expanding!
shorts.coreQuestion: How do you extract the vertex, y-intercept, and x-intercepts from vertex form a(x - h)² + k?

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: Problem #4 features f of x equals negative 5 times the quantity x plus 3 then squared plus 180. It has three parts: y intercept, x intercepts, and vertex!

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: For Part A, find the y intercept by plugging in x equals 0! f of 0 equals negative 5 times 0 plus 3 squared plus 180.

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: 3 squared is 9. Negative 5 times 9 is negative 45. Negative 45 plus 180 equals 135! The y intercept is 0, 135!

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: For Part B, set f of x equal to 0! Subtract 180: negative 180 equals negative 5 times the quantity x plus 3 squared. Divide by negative 5: negative 180 over negative 5 gives 36!

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: Apply the Square Root Property: x plus 3 equals plus or minus the square root of 36, which is plus or minus 6! Subtract 3: x equals negative 3 plus or minus 6.

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: Negative 3 plus 6 is 3, giving 3, 0! Negative 3 minus 6 is negative 9, giving negative 9, 0! And for Part C: vertex form reveals the vertex directly: negative 3, 180!

shorts.title: Exit Ticket #5: Comprehensive Graph Reading: f(x) = x² - 6x + 9
shorts.subtitle: 8-Part Visual Inspection of a Tangent Parabola
shorts.hook: Answer all 8 graph reading questions from vertex to minimum value in one minute!
shorts.coreQuestion: How do you visually determine intercepts, vertex, axis of symmetry, min value, and inputs from a parabola graph?
shorts.mathFocus: \text{Vertex } (3, 0), \; \text{y-int } (0, 9), \; \text{Min Value } 0 \text{ at } x = 3, \; f(2) = 1, \; f(x)=4 \implies x = 1, 5

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: Problem #5 asks us to read the graph of f of x equals x squared minus 6x plus 9 to answer eight key questions! Sora, let's read the graph!

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: Part A: y intercept! Look where the curve crosses the vertical axis: at 0, 9! Part B: x intercept! The curve touches the horizontal axis at 3, 0!

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: Part C: Vertex is that exact turning point: 3, 0! Part D: Axis of Symmetry is the vertical fold line through the vertex: x equals 3!

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: Part E asks: What is the minimum value of f of x? Minimum value always means the lowest y-value, which is 0!

dialogue.speaker: Prof. Park
dialogue.text: Part F asks: At what x value does the minimum occur? That asks for the input location: x equals 3!

dialogue.speaker: TA Sora
dialogue.text: Part G: find f of 2. Look at x equals 2 and trace up to the graph: y equals 1! And Part H: f of x equals 4 when x equals what? Look at height y equals 4: the line hits at x equals 1 and x equals 5! 100% on the exit ticket!
